findings.current: None of them possessed energy as vast as Team Leader Choi’s, but Kim and Song Song were mages, so they were skilled at handling mana and adapted quickly.
findings.defect: “None of them” incorrectly includes Team Leader Choi, directly contradicting the comparison that establishes him as the person with vast energy.
findings.rationale: The comparison 최 팀장처럼 excludes Team Leader Choi from the people who lack energy comparable to his.
findings.replacement: None of the others possessed energy as vast as Team Leader Choi’s, but Kim and Song Song were mages, so they were skilled at handling mana and adapted quickly.
findings.source: 비록 최 팀장처럼 막대한 기운을 품고 있는 사람은 없었지만, 김 집사와 송송이는 마법사답게 마나를 다루는 것에 능숙했고 빠르게 적응했다.

findings.current: If Im Kkeokjeong could resolve the conscious parts of the problem, such as his trauma, he would be able to return to the Guild before long.
findings.defect: “The conscious parts of the problem” is an unnatural literalization that obscures the distinction between his improving physical condition and his remaining psychological issues.
findings.rationale: 의식적인 부분들 refers to mental or psychological obstacles, contrasted here with the physical aftereffects that qi circulation will address.
findings.replacement: If Im Kkeokjeong could overcome the psychological issues, such as his trauma, he would be able to return to the Guild before long.
findings.source: 임꺽정이 트라우마와 같은 의식적인 부분들만 해결한다면, 이른 시일 안에 길드로 복귀할 수 있을 것이다.

findings.current: Lee Jungryong had already drawn the knife hidden up his sleeve, and he was now in a position where he had to pay us for it.
findings.defect: The draft changes 들이댔고 from turning or pressing a concealed blade against someone into merely drawing it, weakening the completed hostile action and its causal connection to the price he must pay.
findings.rationale: 칼을 들이대다 means to hold, press, or turn a knife against a target, not simply to draw one.
findings.replacement: Lee Jungryong had already turned the knife hidden up his sleeve against us, and now he was in a position where he had to pay us the price.
findings.source: 이정룡은 이미 소매에 숨겨 둔 칼을 들이댔고, 그 대가를 우리에게 지불해야 할 처지다.

findings.defect: The generic “instructor” loses the drillmaster sense of 교두 and weakens the joke connecting the new Title to Taekyung working everyone mercilessly.
findings.rationale: 교두 denotes an instructor responsible for drilling and training people, which motivates the following thought about working them to death.
findings.replacement: A martial arts drill instructor, huh.

findings.current: When the guy, who looked kind of dumbfounded, said yes, Lord Fuck laughed like a maniac and walked away going, “Irasshaimase!” and all that shit.
findings.defect: “Dumbfounded” describes a temporary reaction, whereas 얼빵하게 생긴 describes the man as dopey-looking.
findings.rationale: 생긴 explicitly marks this as a description of the man’s appearance rather than his emotional state.
findings.replacement: When the dopey-looking guy said yes, Lord Fuck laughed like a maniac, went, “Irasshaimase!” and all that shit, then walked away.
findings.source: 얼빵하게 생긴 놈이 맞다고 하니까 미친 듯이 웃으면서 이랏샤이마세! ㅇㅈㄹ 하고 감;

findings.defect: The blunt imperative removes the polite request encoded by 만요 and alters the junior speaker’s register toward the person he has just addressed as 형님.
findings.rationale: The source is an abbreviated but polite request, not an order.

findings.current:
“Rows and columns!”

“Rows and colum~ns!”

“Too quiet. Rows and columns!”

“Rows and colum~ns!”
findings.defect: “Rows and columns” is a literal description rather than a natural military-style formation command.
findings.rationale: 오와 열 is used here as a command to form orderly ranks and files, reinforced by the trainees repeating it back in cadence.
findings.replacement:
“Form ranks!”

“Form raaanks!”

“Too quiet. Form ranks!”

“Form raaanks!”
findings.source:
“오와 열.”

“오와 여어얼!”

“목소리가 작다. 오와 열.”

“오와 여어얼!”

findings.current: “Now, follow me in order. Left foot. Left foot.”
findings.defect: The draft omits 입장, the explicit command to enter the Gate, leaving only a vague instruction to follow.
findings.rationale: 입장 specifies entering, while 차례대로 specifies doing so in sequence.
findings.replacement: “Now, follow me inside one at a time. Left foot. Left foot.”
findings.source: “자, 차례대로 나를 따라 입장. 왼발. 왼발.”

findings.current: [^1]: Dooly is the name of a famously mischievous Korean cartoon dinosaur; the line twists a saying about people treating repeated goodwill as their due.
findings.defect: The footnote explains the underlying saying but omits the actual wordplay connecting 호이 to Dooly, so the otherwise opaque reference remains only partially explained.
findings.rationale: The joke substitutes Dooly’s “Hoi” for 호의, meaning goodwill; identifying Dooly merely as a mischievous dinosaur does not convey that linguistic link.
findings.replacement: [^1]: A pun on *houi* (“goodwill”) and Dooly’s catchphrase, “Hoi!” The original saying means that repeated goodwill gets mistaken for an entitlement.

summary: The draft contains two materially altered scene details, one mistranslated physical description, several losses of register or mechanism, and localized terminology and footnote issues.
